after: ## The new media and their role in contemporary society
alt: Cultural optimists Jenkins and Castells see new media as participatory and democratic. Pessimists Keen, Morozov, Zuboff, Pariser and Marxists argue quality falls, activism weakens and a few platforms hold control.
caption: New media widen participation, but unequally and on platforms owned by a few.

after: ## Ownership and control of the media
alt: A grid comparing instrumentalist Marxism, neo-Marxism and pluralism on who controls media content, how control works, and the evidence each uses.
caption: Owners, dominant ideas or audiences: three answers to who controls the media.

after: ## The media, globalisation and popular culture
alt: Cultural imperialism, from Adorno and Horkheimer and Schiller, sees Western media spreading one way. Thussu’s contra-flows, glocalisation and postmodern views show flows in several directions and active audiences.
caption: Global media flows are more complex than a one-way spread of Western culture.

after: ## Selection and presentation of the news
alt: Five steps in making news: gatekeeping, news values, practical factors such as deadlines and press releases, framing, and agenda setting, which shapes the issues the public thinks about.
caption: Each stage filters and shapes what reaches the audience as news.

alt: Key studies of media representation for gender, ethnicity, social class, age, sexuality and disability, from Tuchman and Mulvey to van Dijk, Jones, Cohen and Barnes.
caption: Each group has its own body of evidence on stereotyping and absence.

alt: Six models of media effects arranged from passive to active audiences: hypodermic syringe, cultivation, cultural effects, two-step flow, uses and gratifications, and reception and postmodern views.
caption: Effects models range from a passive audience to one that actively makes meaning.
